subject: Training on customer data opt-out — confirmation and next steps
messages_1_subject: Training on customer data opt-out — request and form
messages_1_body:
Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the call earlier — the demo was helpful. One of our risk reviewers asked for a formal confirmation that Acme Financial data will not be used to train or improve any Redwood public or internal models (training-on-customer-data opt-out). Could you confirm that and share the formal opt-out form?

Also, a few quick clarifying questions from our security team:
- Will any PII be logged in full-text auditor logs that are accessible outside the customer tenancy?
- What is the default data retention period for request/response logs and tokens?
- Can you confirm tenant isolation for KV cache and any prefix caching?

Procurement is looped in for contract language if needed. We're aiming to finish legal review this week.

Thanks,
Jordan
Director of Platform Risk
Acme Financial
messages_2_subject: Re: Training on customer data opt-out — request and form
messages_2_body:
Hi Jordan — great to connect earlier.

Short answers up front:
- Redwood will not use Acme Financial's customer data to train or improve any public models unless you explicitly opt in.
- PII: we do not surface raw PII outside the customer tenancy; access controls prevent cross-tenant visibility. Auditor logs can be configured to redact sensitive fields — we can provide the redaction configuration.
- Retention: default request/response logs are retained 30 days for hosted customers; Dedicated/Private customers can configure retention down to 0 days or longer per contract.
- KV/prefix caching: tenant-isolated; we maintain per-customer namespaces and keys are not shared.

I'm attaching the standard opt-out form (redwood-training-opt-out-form.pdf) and our data-handling checklist (acme-data-handling-checklist.xlsx) for your legal and security teams.

I'll loop in Marissa from Legal and Neha from Compliance to confirm the formal acceptance language and to get a signed copy back to you.

Next steps I propose:
1) You review & sign the opt-out form (we can do DocuSign).
2) We supply a short attestation letter and the redaction config for your SecOps team.
3) If needed, we add contract language (addendum) for the final PO.

Thanks,
Vivek
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
messages_3_subject: FW: Training on customer data opt-out — Acme Financial (please review)
messages_3_body:
Marissa / Neha — forwarding the Acme thread. Jordan from Acme Financial has asked for a formal opt-out (no training) and clarifications on logging/retention/redaction. I attached our standard opt-out form and checklist.

Can Legal/Compliance please:
- Confirm the opt-out form language is sufficient as a binding attestation (or propose brief contract addendum wording).
- Confirm we can provide the attestation letter and the recommended redaction config for their SecOps team.
- If they want DocuSign, happy to send.

Timing: they want to close legal review this week. If you can take a quick look and propose any edits (or sign-off) that would be great.

Thanks,
Vivek
messages_4_subject: Re: Training on customer data opt-out — confirmation and next steps
messages_4_body:
Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear summary and for sending procurement along.

Legal/Compliance have reviewed the attached opt-out form and we can confirm the following:
1) Redwood confirms Acme Financial data will not be used to train or improve any Redwood models (public or internal) for the account identified in the attached form, unless Acme provides explicit written opt-in.
2) We will provide a signed attestation letter on Redwood letterhead once you sign the opt-out form.
3) Retention and logging: hosted default is 30 days; as discussed we can set retention to 0 days or a custom retention period for Dedicated/Private deployments via contract. We will also provide the redaction configuration for your SecOps team (fields we suggest redacting).
4) Tenant isolation: KV and prefix caches are isolated by account and keys are not shared across customers.

Attachments: redwood-training-opt-out-form.pdf (please sign) — we can DocuSign if you prefer (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.net/1234ABC).

If procurement wants contract addendum language, we can provide a short clause to append to the SOW covering training opt-out and retention.

Next steps:
- Jordan / Procurement: sign the attached form or reply confirming you prefer DocuSign.
- Vivek / Redwood: we will return a signed attestation and the redaction config and addendum language if requested.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
thread_notes: Customer requested formal opt-out and clarification on logging/retention; Redwood provided form + legal attestation path; awaiting customer signature (DocuSign option).
